facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Uragasaurus consists of a single anterior dorsal vertebra.
facts.quote: It consists of a single anterior (toward the front) dorsal vertebra.

facts.statement: The holotype vertebra of Uragasaurus was flattened from front to back due to taphonomic compression.
facts.quote: Taphonomic compression has flattened the bone anteroposteriorly (from front to back).

facts.statement: Uragasaurus fossils were found in the lower Phu Kradung Formation in Kalasin Province, northeastern Thailand.
facts.quote: The Uragasaurus fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the lower Phu Kradung Formation (Phu Noi locality), part of the Khorat Group, in Kalasin Province of northeastern Thailand.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Uragasaurus is housed at Mahasarakham University under the accession number PRC 460.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Palaeontological Research and Education Centre (PRC) at Mahasarakham University, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen PRC 460.

facts.statement: Uragasaurus was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Apirut Nilpanapan and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Apirut Nilpanapan and colleagues described Uragasaurus kalasinensis as a new genus and species of mamenchisaurid sauropod based on these fossil remains, establishing PRC 460 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Several other dinosaur bones were found near the holotype but cannot be confidently assigned to Uragasaurus.
facts.quote: A middle cervical vertebra, right cervical rib, two anterior dorsal vertebral neural arches and a mid-posterior (toward the rear) dorsal vertebra, a left coracoid, and a left fibula were found disarticulated but in close association with the holotype of U. kalasinensis.

facts.statement: Uragasaurus is distinguished from other mamenchisaurids by a teardrop-shaped pneumatic fossa at the tip of the transverse processes on its anterior dorsal vertebra.
facts.quote: Nilpanapan et al. (2026) recognized a single autapomorphy (unique derived character) distinguishing Uragasaurus from all other mamenchisaurids: the distal (toward the tip) end of the transverse processes on the anterior dorsal vertebra have a prominent pneumatic fossa in an elongate teardrop shape.

facts.statement: While Uragasaurus itself is known only from a vertebra, its relatives are characterized by greatly elongated necks.
facts.quote: More complete relatives are characterized by their greatly elongated necks.

facts.statement: Uragasaurus is classified as a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Uragasaurus () is an extinct genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Jurassic Phu Kradung Formation of Thailand.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Uragasaurus as an early-diverging member of Mamenchisauridae, after Tienshanosaurus and before Qijianglong.
facts.quote: Uragasaurus was recovered as an early-diverging member of the eusauropod clade Mamenchisauridae, diverging after Tienshanosaurus but before Qijianglong.

facts.statement: The parent group of Uragasaurus is the family Mamenchisauridae.
Uragasaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
Uragasaurus lived between 149.2 and 137.05 million years ago during the Tithonian to Berriasian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Berriasian (149.2 to 137.05 million years ago)

facts.statement: Uragasaurus is the first named member of the family Mamenchisauridae from Thailand.
facts.quote: It is the first member of the family Mamenchisauridae named from Thailand.

facts.statement: It is debated whether other fossil fragments found near the holotype belong to Uragasaurus because they lack diagnostic features.
facts.quote: A middle cervical vertebra, right cervical rib, two anterior dorsal vertebral neural arches and a mid-posterior (toward the rear) dorsal vertebra, a left coracoid, and a left fibula were found disarticulated but in close association with the holotype of U. kalasinensis. They cannot be confidently referred to this species due to the absence of shared or diagnostic anatomical features.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic relationships of Uragasaurus are weakly supported due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil material.
facts.quote: The relationships among mamenchisaurids in their analysis were weakly supported, partly due to the fragmentary nature of some taxa, such as Uragasaurus.

rejected.statement: Uragasaurus is an extinct genus containing only one species, Uragasaurus kalasinensis, known from a single dorsal vertebra.
rejected.quote: The genus contains a single species, Uragasaurus kalasinensis, known from a single dorsal (trunk) vertebra.
